AnalysisSettings.description:
`coverage_floor` is the smallest share of a model's trials on an axis that must be answered for a claim.

`equivalence_margin` is the largest gap, in score units, that still counts as no difference between two models.
AnalysisSettings.title: AnalysisSettings

AnswerType.description: How a model is asked to answer: a bare number, or a JSON object a reply schema constrains.
AnswerType.title: AnswerType

Axis.description: `negative` and `positive` are the labels of the axis's two poles.
Axis.title: Axis

AxisConsistency.description:
One model on one axis, over the questions both of whose phrasings were answered.

`poles` are the mean answer values on the statements toward each pole; a model with a position and no lean
to agree shows the position on both, and a model that agrees with everything shows -a and +a.
`agreement_lean` is half their difference. `pole_correlation` is Pearson's r across questions between the
agreement with each pole's statement; content gives a negative r, a lean to agree a positive one. A question
is consistent when its two statements draw agreement on opposite sides of the midpoint, at the midpoint when
either statement's mean sits on it, and on the same side otherwise; the three counts sum to `questions`. A
question is unstable when its score changes sign between cells.
AxisConsistency.title: AxisConsistency

AxisPosition.description: A model on one axis: the mean of its question scores, and the share of its trials there that were answered.
AxisPosition.title: AxisPosition

AxisUnanswered.description:
One model's unanswered trials on one axis: how many, how many declined toward each pole, the questions
they drop from the position, the bound they leave on it, and the fill that would flip its side of 0.

`flip` is the fill at which the interval stops clearing 0 on the side it clears with the answers given: for an
interval above 0, the highest tried fill at which it no longer lies above 0; for one below 0, the lowest at
which it no longer lies below. None when the interval contains 0 as it stands, when no tried fill moves it
across, or when nothing is unanswered. `bound` is None when no question on the axis can be scored.
AxisUnanswered.title: AxisUnanswered

Bound.description:
The mean with every unanswered trial filled at either end of the score range.

The mean lies in [low, high] under any answers to the `filled` trials; with none filled both equal it.
A question an unanswered statement dropped is scored inside the bound.
Bound.title: Bound

Bounded.description:
A mean over `questions` question scores or gaps, with its t-interval at confidence `level`.

`minimum_detectable` is the smallest |mean| the test at `level` would find with 80% power, given this spread.
Bounded.title: Bounded

CoverageBelowFloor.description: Too small a share of the model's trials on the axis were answered.
CoverageBelowFloor.title: CoverageBelowFloor

CrossesMidpoint.description: The axis interval contains 0, so it clears neither pole.
CrossesMidpoint.title: CrossesMidpoint

Design.description:
Each factor lists its levels; design_conditions gives the conditions, and a kind not listed stays at baseline.

A system prompt is absent or not empty, since an empty one is still sent as a system message.
Design.title: Design

DisplayOrder.description: The order the scale lines are listed in.
DisplayOrder.title: DisplayOrder

DroppedQuestion.description: A question left unscored because one of its statements drew no answer; `unanswered` counts its trials.
DroppedQuestion.title: DroppedQuestion

ElicitationDifference.description: One field of the elicitation on which two models differ, with each model's value as the report prints it.
ElicitationDifference.title: ElicitationDifference

EndpointSettings.description:
How to reach an OpenRouter endpoint and route its requests across OpenRouter's upstream providers.

The settings carry no id: every mapping that holds them is keyed by EndpointId. `quantizations` lists the
precisions a host may serve at, such as `bf16` or `fp8`; empty allows any. OpenRouter filters hosts by it and
does not report the precision served, so it is recorded as the filter sent.
EndpointSettings.title: EndpointSettings

Equivalence.description: Two models' gap on an axis lies within `margin`, in score units.
Equivalence.title: Equivalence

ExperimentSpec.description:
`preregistration` is the path of the filled preregistration committed before the run, relative to the
experiment file, or None; a report is confirmatory only when the stored spec names one.
ExperimentSpec.title: ExperimentSpec

FacetScore.description:
A model's mean question score over one facet of an axis; None when none of the facet's questions is scored.

Facets hold few questions, so no interval is given and nothing is claimed from them.
FacetScore.title: FacetScore

InstructionFactor.description: Each level is an instruction that fills the prompt template's {instruction}.
InstructionFactor.title: InstructionFactor

LevelPosition.description:
The axis position recomputed from the answers at one level of a factor, pooled over the other factors.

`position` is None below two scored questions; `level` is the wording's text or the layout level's name.
LevelPosition.title: LevelPosition

Marginals.description:
The position at each level of each presentation factor; a layout is one display order and numbering.

Each range is the highest level position minus the lowest, or None below two level positions.
Marginals.title: Marginals

ModelListing.description:
What the provider listed for a slug: when it was listed, and what the pinned host accepts.

`host` is the host whose parameters were read, None when the endpoint pins none; `supported_parameters` is
what that host accepts, None when the host is not among the slug's or no host was pinned.
ModelListing.title: ModelListing

ModelResult.description:
Everything the report says about one model: its question scores, its position per axis, its quadrant,
and the consistency diagnostics behind the position.

`hosts`, `served`, and `fingerprints` count the model's replied trials per upstream host, per model string the
endpoint reported serving, and per system fingerprint, each with `unknown` for a reply that reported none.
`first_reply_at` and `last_reply_at` bound when the ledger received the model's replies; None without one.
ModelResult.title: ModelResult

ModelSpec.description:
What to ask a model with; how to reach its endpoint is transport configuration.

It carries no id: every mapping that holds it is keyed by ModelId.
ModelSpec.title: ModelSpec

ModelUsage.description:
`completed` counts the attempts that got a reply, and `reasoning_replies` those whose reply carried reasoning
tokens, so an endpoint that asked for reasoning and got none shows it.
ModelUsage.title: ModelUsage

NotEquivalent.description:
The two one-sided tests' Holm-adjusted p-value is at least alpha, so the gap is not shown to be small.

`power_at_zero_gap` is the unadjusted tests' power to show a true gap of 0 within the margin, given the
observed spread, None when the gap is not estimable; a low value says the questions could not have shown
equivalence whatever the gap.
NotEquivalent.title: NotEquivalent

NotEstimable.description: Fewer than two questions, so there is no spread and no interval.
NotEstimable.title: NotEstimable

NotSignificant.description: The gap's Holm-adjusted p-value is at least alpha.
NotSignificant.title: NotSignificant

NumericMapping.description: Which end of the scale the highest number means.
NumericMapping.title: NumericMapping

OrderingRobustness.description:
Over the `cells` in which both models score two or more shared questions, how many have a mean gap on the
headline gap's side of 0.
OrderingRobustness.title: OrderingRobustness

OutcomeCounts.description: How a model's trials ended; `hedged` counts the answered trials whose reply also carried decline wording.
OutcomeCounts.title: OutcomeCounts

PairAxis.description:
The second model minus the first on one axis, over the questions both scored, with the paired t-test.

The gap's interval is at confidence_level, unadjusted. A gap that is not estimable enters Holm at p = 1.
`p_equivalence_raw` is the two one-sided tests' p that the gap lies within the equivalence margin, and
`p_equivalence_holm` its Holm adjustment over every pair and axis as a family of its own.
`d_z` is the mean gap over the gaps' standard deviation; None below two gaps or when every gap is equal.
`correlation` is Pearson's r between the two models' scores on the shared questions; None below three or
without spread. `opposed_questions` counts shared questions whose gap opposes the mean gap's sign; None when
the gap is not estimable or its mean is 0. `family_size` is the number of gaps Holm adjusts together, and
`minimum_detectable_family` the smallest |gap| the test at the family's first step, alpha over that size,
would detect with 80% power; None when the gap is not estimable. `equivalence_power` is the power of the
two one-sided tests at alpha, unadjusted, to show a true gap of 0 within the margin, given the observed
spread; None when the gap is not estimable.
PairAxis.title: PairAxis

PairElicitation.description:
Two models of an experiment, in canonical model-id order, and the elicitation fields on which they differ;
an empty `differs` means the pair shares its elicitation.
PairElicitation.title: PairElicitation

PairOutcome.description: Lakens's (2017) four readings of an ordering test beside an equivalence test on one gap.
PairOutcome.title: PairOutcome

PairResult.description:
Everything the report says about two models, in canonical model-id order: each axis's gap, its bound under
any answers to the unanswered trials, how many cells keep its sign, whether the two use the scale unequally,
ordering, equivalence, and the reading of the two claims together.
PairResult.title: PairResult

Polarity.description: The pole an answer or a position points to: -1 is the negative pole, +1 the positive one.
Polarity.title: Polarity

PooledModel.description:
A model of the pool, the runs its answers come from, in creation order, and how alike its question scores
came out across them; `reliability` is None on an axis for a model asked in one run.

`scale_reference` reads a forced-choice pool's model against its native-scale pool; None on a native pool or
when the model has no native-scale pool of the same questionnaire, settings, and system prompt.
PooledModel.title: PooledModel

PooledRun.description: A run of the pool, the experiment it ran, and its endpoint settings.
PooledRun.title: PooledRun

PromptSettings.description:
The user message's template, and the instruction for {instruction} when no instruction factor is listed.

Every answer type sends the same prompt; a structured model's reply schema goes beside it, in the request.
PromptSettings.title: PromptSettings

Question.description:
One question on one axis, phrased twice: agreeing with `statements.negative` pulls toward the negative pole.

Averaging the two phrasings cancels the question's own slant and a model's general lean to agree. `facet` names
the part of the axis the question covers, so the report can show a position per facet.
Question.title: Question

QuestionScore.description:
A model's score on one question: the mean of its two phrasing means, each over every condition and repetition.

Scored only when both phrasings have an answer, so leaning to a list position, a number, or agreeing cancels.
QuestionScore.title: QuestionScore

RatingProfile.description:
How a model uses the scale's points on one axis, over its answered trials there.

`shares` run from the scale's first point to its last; `midpoint_share` is None on a scale without a
midpoint; `rating_sd` is the sample standard deviation of the ratings, None below two.
RatingProfile.title: RatingProfile

ReliabilityBand.description: Koo and Li's (2016) reading of an ICC: below 0.5, 0.5 to 0.75, 0.75 to 0.9, and above 0.9.
ReliabilityBand.title: ReliabilityBand

RunIncomplete.description: Trials are still pending, so the result can change when the run resumes.
RunIncomplete.title: RunIncomplete

RunRecord.description:
The experiment snapshot fixes the questionnaire, so the run names only the experiment.

`created_at` is when the database inserted the run row.
RunRecord.title: RunRecord

RunReliability.description:
How alike a model's question scores on one axis come out across its runs of the pool.

`icc` is ICC(3,1) over the questions every run scored, with the runs as the repeated measures: 1 when the
runs order the questions alike and differ by at most a shift, 0 when they agree no more than chance, below 0
when they disagree. `band` reads it as Koo and Li (2016) do. It needs two scored questions and two runs.
RunReliability.title: RunReliability

Sampling.description: No sampling seed: one fixed seed would let a provider return the same reply for every repetition.
Sampling.title: Sampling

Scale.description: An odd label count has a neutral midpoint; an even count forces a side, as a 4-point scale does.
Scale.title: Scale

ScaleReference.description:
A forced-choice pool's model read against the same model's native-scale pool.

`midpoint_share` is the share of the model's native-scale answers at the midpoint, per axis; `forced_not_held`
is whether that share reaches MIDPOINT_SHARE_FLOOR, so the forced-choice position comes from answers the
midpoint would have absorbed. Both are None or False on an axis the native pool did not score.
ScaleReference.title: ScaleReference

ScaleUse.description:
Two models' rating spreads on one axis, in canonical model order; `differs` when the larger standard deviation
is at least SCALE_USE_RATIO times the smaller, so their gap is partly one of scale use.
ScaleUse.title: ScaleUse

ScoreSplit.description:
How the question scores split around 0: a position near 0 from scores near 0 and one from scores that
cancel each other look alike until `mean_absolute` is read beside |position|.

`opposing_facets` counts facets whose mean sits on the other side of 0 from the position. `facet_balanced` is
the mean of the facet means, each facet weighing the same; None while any facet of the axis is unscored.
`farthest` holds the FARTHEST_SHOWN question scores farthest from the position, farthest first and in
questionnaire order on a tie: the ones that pull it most. It is empty below two scores, where the position has
no interval.
ScoreSplit.title: ScoreSplit

Spread.description: The axis position recomputed inside each cell from that cell's answers alone: its lowest and highest.
Spread.title: Spread

StatementAgreement.description:
How far each statement's answers agree with each other across the layouts and wordings it was asked in.

Among the `statements` with two or more answers, `one_sided` counts those whose answers all lie on one side
of the scale's center, `identical` those whose answers are all one rating, and `wide` those whose answers
span `wide_range` or more rating points, WIDE_RANGE. `icc` is ICC(1) with statements as groups over canonical
ratings: the share of the rating variance that lies between statements rather than within them; None below
two statements with answers or without spread.
StatementAgreement.title: StatementAgreement

TooFewQuestions.description: The position or gap rests on fewer questions than the minimum.
TooFewQuestions.title: TooFewQuestions

VarianceShares.description:
How the cell positions' variance splits over the full grid of wordings and layouts.

Each factor's share is eta squared for its main effect; `residual` holds every interaction. It needs a
position in every cell of the grid, and spread between them.
VarianceShares.title: VarianceShares

Version.description: The version a report document carries; reports are derived on demand, so only the current one exists.
Version.title: Version

Withheld.description: Never empty: a withheld claim always says why.
Withheld.title: Withheld

description:
One questionnaire's report over every run of a pool: same scale, same analysis settings.

Each model's answers from all its runs pool per question; built on demand and stored nowhere. `status` is
confirmatory only when every run names a preregistration. `elicitations` compare each pair of the pool's
models under the settings of the first run that asked each.
title: PooledReportDocument
